title: Introduce ortho-fuse attention kernel with windowed-rotary indexing and prefetch coordinator
author: Marina Alvarez
release_notes: Adds 'ortho-fuse' fused attention kernel optimized for windowed rotary indexing and a prefetch coordinator that warms KV cache and improves continuous batching. Expect ~15-25% throughput improvements on long-sequence workloads and reduced P50 latency. No public API changes.
description:
Context and motivation: This PR implements a new attention microkernel ('ortho-fuse') that orthogonally fuses QK computation with rotary index transforms and introduces a small prefetch coordinator inside the serving scheduler to warm the KV cache and steer continuous batching. Motivation: long sequence workloads (4k-16k) were suffering from KV warmup stalls and Q-K/rotary roundtrip overheads that prevented the existing Flash variants from fully leveraging kernel-level data locality. The ortho-fuse design packs rotary index remapping into the same GPU tile as QK matmul when sequence windows permit, enabling a single pass over activation buffers and fewer global memory reads.

What changed (high-level): 1) New CUDA microkernel 'ortho_fuse_kernel.cu' with fused QK + rotary remap + softmax-shared workspace path. 2) Kernel registry and heuristic selector to choose ortho-fuse for window-aligned requests; falls back to flash/standard kernels for misaligned widths. 3) Prefetch coordinator in serving scheduler that pre-warms KV caches for active sessions and implements a lightweight KV 'peek' to populate hot lanes before model execution. 4) KV cache manager additions to support epoch-based warming and safe concurrent evictions with minimal locking. 5) Continuous batching adjustments: soft-enqueue policy tweak to avoid head-of-line blocking when prefetch is in-flight. 6) Tests, docs, and benchmarks.

Commits (summary): - Add ortho-fuse kernel implementation and unit integration (commit: 'kernel: add ortho-fuse fused qk+rotary path') - Add heuristic selector for ortho-fuse based on seq_len/window alignment ('runtime: ortho-fuse selector') - Scheduler: prefetch coordinator and KV peek API ('serving: introduce prefetch coordinator & kv peek') - KV: epoch warming and concurrent eviction fixes ('kv: safe warming and eviction') - Continuous batching tweaks and tests ('scheduler: soft-enqueue tweak to reduce HL blocking') - Benchmarks and perf doc ('bench: ortho-fuse perf notebook', 'docs: ortho-fuse performance notes')

Files changed (representative): runtimes/cuda/ortho_fuse_kernel.cu, runtimes/cuda/ortho_fuse_kernel.cuh, runtimes/cuda/kernel_registry.py, serving/scheduler/prefetch_coordinator.py, serving/kv/cache_manager.py, serving/kv/kv_peek.h, serving/scheduler/continuous_batcher.py, benchmarks/attn/ortho_fuse_bench.ipynb, tests/attn/test_ortho_fuse.py, docs/perf/ortho-fuse.md, tools/perf/compare_runs.sh, ci/perf-run.yaml, examples/ortho-fuse/README.md, CHANGELOG.md

Benchmarks: Microbenchmarks on p4d.24xlarge with fp16 models: - 8k seq, batch 1: throughput +18% tokens/sec, p50 latency -12% - 4k seq, batch 2: throughput +22%, p50 latency -14% - 16k seq streaming (sliding windows): throughput +25% with ortho-fuse windowing vs baseline flash-attn+separate-rotary. Memory: small increase (~4%) in peak scratch due to fused workspace allocation but net token-cost reduction. Real workload A (multi-turn retrieval): end-to-end latency 10% lower and 17% cost-per-token improvement by reducing KV re-reads.

Compatibility and fallback: The runtime selects ortho-fuse only when window alignment and headroom checks pass. Otherwise we fall back to the existing Flash kernels. We also expose a config flag 'enable_ortho_fuse' under runtime.experimental to allow staged rollouts. No changes to public API surface.

Testing and CI: Unit tests added for correctness vs baseline softmax outputs and rotary-aligned indices. Integration tests validate KV peek semantics under concurrent warmup/eviction. CI status: build: pass, unit-tests: pass, lint: pass, perf-run: initially flaky (missing perf artifact on first run) -> rerun and pass. Perf regression gateway shows improvements; no regressions.

Discussion and review notes: - Anil Kapoor: requested tighter bounds on numeric deviation vs baseline; asked to include differential test across sequence lengths. Response: added randomized numeric-diff test with tolerance 1e-3 and summary table in tests/attn/test_ortho_fuse.py. - Sofia Martinez: asked to ensure prefetch respects tenant isolation and does not leak KV slices. Response: prefetch coordinator uses session-scoped peeks and never exposes raw KV contents, and we added an audit log event for prefetch triggers. - Ethan Cole: suggested making the selector more conservative for small batches; implemented heuristic to require min_batch_tokens >= 512 before enabling ortho-fuse. - Performance engineering (review thread): suggested reducing shared workspace allocation; we added an allocation pool per-stream and reclaimed between calls.

Known limitations: - Ortho-fuse benefits are most pronounced when sequence windows align to kernel tile widths; pathological misaligned patterns will fall back to baseline and see no change. - Small-batch workloads under 512 tokens may see neutral or marginally worse latency due to additional prefetch coordination overhead if misapplied; selector prevents this.

Rollout plan: merged to main behind runtime.experimental flag. Post-merge: staged canary rollout to Dedicated clusters, monitor p50/p95 and KV miss rates. Ramp to hosted API only after 2 weeks of canary telemetry and no perf regressions.

Merge details: PR merged by Marina Alvarez on 2026-03-05 via squash. Linear: ENG-1489 closed. Release notes: add ortho-fuse kernel to perf improvements list.

If follow-ups are needed: - Fine-tune selector thresholds per-model family (TODO: ENG-1591) - Investigate lowering scratch allocation further for memory-constrained GPUs (follow-up perf PR).
